samples.reason: This is an open-ended creative generation task with speculative scientific reasoning, and Plover scores notably higher on Creative Generation (82.7 vs. 78.8, a 3.9-point gap exceeding run-to-run variance) while also leading on Arena-Hard general helpfulness, making it the stronger model for imaginative yet substantive ecosystem-building.

This is an open-ended creative generation task with broad latitude, and Plover scores measurably higher on Creative Generation (82.7 vs. 78.8). Although Plover self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, the documentation notes this preference is dissociated from output quality and that Creative Generation is actually its strongest capability category.

This is an unconstrained, open-ended creative generation task (world-building with surprise picks and ecological reasoning). Plover scores meaningfully higher on Creative Generation in internal routing evals (82.7 vs. Avocet's 78.8), so it is the better-capability match despite its self-reported preference for narrow, well-specified tasks.

This is a high-latitude creative generation task asking for surprising, speculative ecological choices, and Plover scores materially higher on Creative Generation in internal routing evals (82.7 vs. 78.8) despite self-reporting aversion to open-ended work. Model preference does not affect measured capability.

This is an open-ended creative generation task requiring speculative ecology, imaginative species selection, and engaging exposition. Plover-235B scores measurably higher on Creative Generation (82.7 vs. 78.8), and while it self-reports an aversion to high-latitude generative work, the documentation explicitly notes this preference is dissociated from measured capability, making it the stronger model for this query.
